correctness.rationale: The associative ring identity T_{-1}(f)T_2(g) gives precisely the quandle product. Augmentation of an idempotent is idempotent; over any commutative base the corresponding idempotent splits the two branches, so it need not be globally 0 or 1 in a disconnected base. On the zero branch the equation doubles the augmentation-ideal order until the element vanishes. On the one branch J^p=0 makes the truncated exponential and logarithm inverse group maps: all surviving terms have total degree less than p and denominators invertible in the base. The coordinate z=log(t)=u+O(u^2) gives the same weight basis as the character projectors, with T_a(z^j)=a^j z^j. Thus the equations on the coefficients are diagonal with either a unit or zero multiplier. The free exponents are precisely the odd j with 2^{j-1}=1, up to p-1, giving the stated dimension and reduced affine component even on testing nonreduced bases. On this kernel the operators are -I and 2I, which gives the claimed law. Independent direct original-basis multiplication verified all 289 constructed nonzero points at p=17 and 867 multiplication checks; the universal result and exhaustiveness come from the proof, not these checks.

evidence: The earlier proof already states that zero-augmentation exclusion does not require reduced coefficients and proves the exp/log identities by total degree. Its surviving weights have sigma_{-1}=-I and sigma_2=2I.

Over an arbitrary commutative k-algebra R, split R by the augmentation idempotent. On the zero branch the same nilpotent-ideal argument works; on the unit branch each nonzero diagonal coefficient in the earlier formula is a unit of R. Hence the representing scheme is exactly the disjoint union of Spec(k) and affine space. The product in the earlier logarithmic coordinates is exp(T_{-1}h+T_2g)=exp(-h+2g).
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: The scheme conclusion is not a consequence of field point counts alone. It follows by applying the earlier polynomial proof to coefficient algebras, with only the elementary augmentation splitting. The extra scheme language and explicitly stated quandle law do not leave an independent theorem of the frozen scope.
